messages:
anya: heads up — customer ACME corp seeing repeated 502s on hosted inference after model swap at ~16:12 UTC. ticket #C-7321. request path /v1/hosted/generate, spikes align with large guest identifiers in headers. @oliver @raj can you take a look?
infra-bot: alert: envoy-ambassador-eu1 reported increased 502 rate for service hosted-api (15m avg +4.8% over baseline) — sample trace ids: trace=9f1a2b3c, trace=4c8d2e01
anya: repro notes: quick curl reproduces for us. below sample (sensitive bits redacted):
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" \ 
  -H "X-Guest-Id: 7f3a9c...<very-long-string>...ff01" \ 
  -d '{"prompt":"hi"}' \ 
  https://hosted-api.redwood.ai/v1/hosted/generate
```
oliver: thanks. can you paste the raw response body + the envoy upstream log line for one of the failed traces? also which envoy/ambassador deploy hash is running on the node that served the failed requests?
anya: paste from client capture (trimmed):
```
> HTTP/2 502
> server: envoy
> content-length: 143
> x-redwood-trace: 9f1a2b3c

{"error":"upstream connection reset","upstream":"stream-router-ambassador","req_id":"9f1a2b3c"}
```
anya: envoy log snippet from node host-amb-22 (time 2025-11-20T16:12:43Z):
```
[warning] [upstream] 2025-11-20T16:12:43Z upstream read error: connection reset by peer, connection_id=0x7f4b3, route=hosted-api, trace=9f1a2b3c
```
raj: :eyes: looks like upstream (stream-router/ambassador) is resetting on large header pressure. can you confirm header sizes? what is `X-Guest-Id` length in the failing request?
anya: `X-Guest-Id` length for failing samples ~7.3k chars. typical values are <1k. reproduced locally by pumping header length and seeing same 502.
leo: probable suspects: envoy `max_request_headers_kb` limit or ambassador/nginx proxy buffer settings. also some recent billing change appended long tenant metadata to guest id, fyi. Did we roll anything to stream-router at 16:10–16:15?
oliver: checking deploy history... stream-router/ambassador rolled 16:09 UTC to hash `a1b2c3d4` with new header enrichment in the rewrite filter. that likely concatenates billing tenant tag into `X-Guest-Id`.
raj: quick mitigation options: 1) revert header enrichment in stream-router (hotfix) 2) increase envoy `max_request_headers_kb` for ambassador listeners 3) add header truncation in frontend ingress as temporary safe-guard. which is lowest-impact?
anya: for now option 3 looks quickest. I pushed a small ingress annotation to drop `X-Guest-Id` beyond 2k chars on canary nodes. initial roll to 10% shows error rate drop ~80% on canary traffic.
support-bot: ticket #C-7321 updated: mitigation applied -> header truncation canary 10% at 16:28 UTC, customer notified.
oliver: good. next steps: revert enrichment in stream-router and create a small canary to validate payloads. raj — can you run a config diff to ensure no envoy listener change required post-revert?
raj: will do. also scheduling follow-up: increase `max_request_headers_kb` from 60 -> 128 on ambassador listeners in eu1 as a targeted safety net. will coordinate with SRE to avoid memory blowup.
anya: added repro steps to ticket: 1) send request with `X-Guest-Id` length ~7k -> 502 2) inspect response body for `upstream connection reset` 3) check envoy log for upstream read error and matching trace id. included sample curl and trace ids.
leo: capture notes: please also grep for `connection reset by peer` in stream-router logs around 16:12 to confirm server-side OOM or accept backlog drop. could be worker thread rejecting large headers.
oliver: ops note: we need a postmortem if revert doesn't fully mitigate. record timeline, deploy hash, config changes, and customer impact. please attach CPU/mem graphs for stream-router pods during spike.
anya: confirmed: stream-router pods showed resident memory bump + open file descriptors spike correlated to header processing. adding those graphs to ticket.
raj: I'm pushing the revert to staging now. will promote to canary once green. ETA canary 30m.
anya: customer reply: they see improvement on canary, asked for ETA to full fix. I told them tentative 2–4 hours pending canary results.
support-bot: follow-up: reminder to tag SRE and Product for billing metadata change review.
oliver: good triage. add retrospective item: validate header growth introduced by middleware and add safety cap in router. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
